summary:
Don't Mess Up Mars is a pixel-art game in which a young player runs a Mars town, New Hope, for 7 sols while the President is away. The player walks around the colony and balances three resources (energy, oxygen and food) plus the colonists' health. There is never enough power for everything: running the oxygen machine, the greenhouse lights, the heater and the radiation shield at the same time drains the battery, so every choice has a cost.

The dangers come from real NASA data. Solar flares are real events from NASA's DONKI space weather database, and each sol's temperatures, including the freezing nights, are real measurements from the Curiosity rover. Dust storms, breakdowns and two-sided decisions make every game different.

An "explore and learn" mode adds real space hardware to discover. Experts teach the basic facts, and at the Shop of Wisdom the player must reason from those facts to answer a question and win a prize. A lost game ends gently and explains what to try next time, so failure teaches instead of punishing.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

The player is the Operator of a Mars colony for 7 sols (Martian days). They walk around a top-down town, switch machines on and off, repair breakdowns, talk to colonists and make decisions. Solar panels make power only by day, so the battery must last the night. The oxygen machine, greenhouse lights, heater and radiation shield all compete for the same power.

HOW IT USES NASA DATA

- Solar flares are real events from NASA's DONKI database. A flare forces the player to power the radiation shield.

- Daily high and low temperatures are real Curiosity rover (REMS) measurements. The coldest real nights become "freezing nights" that need the heater.

- The oxygen machine is based on the MOXIE experiment, and the greenhouse on NASA's Veggie plant experiments on the International Space Station.

LEARNING

On some sols a "?" appears on the map: a real piece of space hardware such as the Apollo Moon buggy, the Moon mirror, the Ingenuity helicopter or Curiosity's radiation detector. An expert explains the basic facts. Then the Shop of Wisdom asks a question whose answer was never stated, so the player has to reason it out from what they learned. Right answers win resources and fill a Discovery Notebook.

DESIGN CHOICES

- Language for ages 7 to 12, with short sentences and no frightening content. If the colony fails, everyone is safe in a shelter and the game suggests what to try next time.

- Every game is different: storms, breakdowns, decisions and side quests are shuffled.

- Mouse and keyboard controls, a pause menu and adjustable text speed.

TOOLS

Godot 4 engine and GDScript. Real data is embedded in the game, so it runs offline.
